details: Tensions between the United States and Iran have sharply escalated after President Trump declared a ceasefire "over," leading to renewed US military strikes and Iranian threats to disrupt oil shipments through the crucial Strait of Hormuz. This escalation has caused oil prices to surge by approximately 6%, fueling global inflation concerns and triggering a "risk-off" sentiment across broader financial markets. Consequently, Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies have experienced declines, with Bitcoin trading around $62,000 after falling from earlier highs. The minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest policy meeting also highlighted worries that elevated energy prices could complicate the inflation outlook, potentially leading to prolonged restrictive monetary policy, further impacting speculative assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: US-Iran Conflict Escalates, Dampening Crypto Market Sentiment

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has reduced its 2026 world economic growth forecast to 3%, citing the fallout from the ongoing conflict involving Iran as a primary factor. Despite strong demand for artificial intelligence (AI) partially mitigating the energy shock caused by the geopolitical tensions, the IMF warns that US inflation could remain elevated until late 2027. This indicates persistent inflationary pressures beyond immediate supply disruptions, suggesting a challenging economic environment that typically leads to reduced investor appetite for riskier assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: IMF Lowers 2026 Global Growth Forecast Amid Iran War Fallout
